claims.statement: Generic MCP connections are owned in three scopes: instance-wide, workspace, and personal-user; an agent run loads them in instance-to-workspace-to-user order, and a later same-named connection replaces the earlier connection entirely.

Instance and workspace MCP dashboard APIs are admin-gated, while personal MCP APIs use the current session subject; list and save responses expose public connection records rather than encrypted credential fields, and header revelation is a separate no-store response.

MCP connection updates require an HTTPS URL without embedded credentials, fragments, or secret-like query keys; validate headers; encrypt supplied headers and client secrets; and permit only client-credentials OAuth that is not combined with an Authorization header.
Saved MCP credentials can be reused only from the previous record in the same scope, and changing a connection URL while implicitly retaining existing authentication headers is rejected.
Generic MCP and Notion tools are loaded concurrently only for non-local, non-summary runs with a known credential scope, making their absence non-fatal to agent construction.

Generic MCP discovery is limited to enabled connections with selected allowed tools, has a 30-second deadline, follows paginated catalogs while rejecting repeated cursors and duplicate names, and caches catalogs for 600 seconds by source namespace, connection name, and revision.

An MCP tool wrapper rereads its named connection at invocation and refuses execution when its source scope, endpoint, transport, enabled state, or allowlist no longer match the load-time definition, so edits or deletion revoke already loaded tools.
When a generic MCP source cannot be listed, loading returns no MCP tools rather than exposing a lower-precedence connection; an individual discovery failure only removes that server's tools.

MCP provider and token traffic is restricted to the configured HTTPS origin, does not follow redirects or environment proxies, requires public DNS-resolved addresses, and pins a validated address with the original TLS hostname.

Client-credentials MCP OAuth decrypts its secret for token acquisition, caches credentials by source namespace and connection configuration, refreshes before expiry, and retries exactly once on a 401; the cache key isolates otherwise identical credentials owned by different users.

Notion is a separate personal OAuth-backed hosted MCP integration at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp: OAuth metadata endpoints are accepted only on that HTTPS host and its stored access, refresh, and dynamic-client secrets are encrypted under the user's credential namespace.

Notion tool loading requires the private credential owner and wraps discovered schemas with required on_behalf_of; each invocation resolves the participant, verifies that private ownership again, obtains a fresh token, rebuilds the named MCP tool, and fails with reconnect guidance if authorization is unavailable.

Notion credentials refresh expired tokens under a per-login lock and remove a stored connection when refresh reports reauthorization is required; lookup is fail-soft so a credential/store failure removes the optional capability instead of failing the run.
LangSmith LLM Gateway routing is centrally applied by make_model after workspace settings resolve gateway_enabled; a boolean workspace value overrides the environment default, while None inherits it.

Gateway routing supports openai, anthropic, baseten, fireworks, and google_genai, prefers LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY over LANGSMITH_API_KEY, and falls back to direct provider calls when the provider is unsupported or no LangSmith key is available.

LANGSMITH_PROJECT identifies the LangSmith project used for tracing, trace links, cost lookups, and feedback; trace URL generation is best effort and returns no link if tenant or project resolution is unavailable.
Dashboard HTTP tracing renames the active Datadog root span after routing to the HTTP method and route path, including when an endpoint raises, so mounted dashboard traffic can be grouped by route.

Focused tests exercise MCP source replacement and no-fallback behavior, OAuth credential lifecycle and redaction, transport origin safety, workspace tool revocation and caching, and Notion per-call credential refresh.
